mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise from their current depressed levels, weekday trip chaining into commercial areas increases and RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks. The signal should be visible first in commuting-related series, then in retail visits.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain far below baseline in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over the next 28 days despite a concurrent rise in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT relative to the snapshot.

mechanism_narrative: A further weekly drop in TRANSIT below its current level reduces discretionary downtown shopping access and lowers RETAIL_REC within one to two weeks. The mechanism fails if retail stays flat while transit keeps falling.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 3 points week-on-week from an already sub-baseline level
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is around -48% to -51% across the snapshot weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT declines further but RETAIL_REC is not lower on a 1-2 week lag than in the prior four-week window.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS rebounds sharply above its recent trough, weekend substitute recreation pulls spending away from retail centers and pushes RETAIL_REC down over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest if PARKS stays elevated for multiple weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 20 points from the prior week after having been below 15 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 45.7 to 11.6 and then rebounded to 22.4 in the snapshot
failure_condition: A sustained PARKS rebound above the trigger is followed by no reduction in RETAIL_REC relative to the prior four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain suppressed, people consolidate errands locally and avoid destination shopping, keeping RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks. This mechanism requires persistent home-based activity rather than a one-week fluctuation.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is above baseline while WORKPLACES remain well below baseline
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL remains above baseline and WORKPLACES remain depressed, but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent improvement in GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC indicates broader household out-of-home activity that spills into shopping trips, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The signal should be positive only when both series move up together.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is less negative than WORKPLACES and TRANSIT in the snapshot
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM improves or remains near baseline but RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-28-day mean within four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week worsening in TRANSIT after a brief recovery is a short-lag warning of renewed mobility restraint, and RETAIL_REC falls within one week. The claim fails if transit noise does not translate into retail weakness immediately.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT reverses downward after a weekly increase and ends below -45
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -51.3 to -47.7 in the snapshot
failure_condition: TRANSIT turns down as specified but RETAIL_REC is not lower in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: In warmer-weather weeks, a PARKS level above its recent baseline shifts leisure time outdoors and suppresses mall and high-street visits, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks. The effect should appear only when PARKS remains above its recent average rather than bouncing for one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays above 20 for at least two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is elevated relative to baseline despite recent volatility
failure_condition: PARKS remains above 20 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not fall below its prior four-week mean over the following month.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES recover while RESIDENTIAL eases from its elevated level, the commute-and-shop pattern strengthens and RETAIL_REC rises over the next two to four weeks. The mechanism is invalid when work mobility improves without any drop in residential staying-home time.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -35 while RESIDENTIAL falls below 11
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -42.0 to -37.1 while RESIDENTIAL stayed above baseline
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises and RESIDENTIAL falls through the trigger band, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 28 days.
